look_here_first: Low annual with axillary flower clusters from base to top; the cluster axes become thick, inflated and hard at maturity, with uniquely keeled flower bracts.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays-local source; Kew accepts species native from Oklahoma through Texas to Mexico.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Installed for visual learning; only current native-range evidence should feed native metrics.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Amaranthaceae/Amaranthus: alternate petiolate leaves and dense clusters of tiny unisexual flowers. Habit, plant sex, hairiness, nodal spines, cluster position, bract/tepal form, and fruit dehiscence are high-value characters.
best_field_traits: axillary clusters from base to top
morphology_keys.comparison_training: The hardened swollen cluster axes and keeled bracts are the key. Much lower and more axillary-clustered than tall Palmer or redroot pigweed.
